---
title: "Switching off"
subtitle: "Stopping the filter without removing it."
description: "How the enabled option turns the social filter off, which values it accepts, and what stays in the head once it is off."
---

`enabled` turns the filter off for a whole project or for one deck.
It is the only option the filter reads through the extension schema, so the default the schema declares applies to it.

That default is `true`.
A deck that never writes `enabled` gets the tags.

## Turning the filter off

Write `enabled` under `extensions.social`:

```yaml
title: "The Grammar of Graphics Assembles"
site-url: "https://example.com/my-talk/"
image: "assets/social-card.png"
filters:
  - social
extensions:
  social:
    enabled: false
```

The filter then writes no tag at all.
Put the same block in `_quarto.yml` to turn the filter off for every deck in a project.

## Which values the option accepts

The schema declares `enabled` as a boolean.
Four spellings resolve to a boolean:

- `true` and `false`, written as bare YAML booleans.
- `"true"` and `"false"`, written as quoted strings.

::: {.callout-warning}

## `yes`, `no`, `0` and `1` leave the filter running

Pandoc reads each of these four as a string, and the schema refuses a string for a boolean.
The render reports the value and carries on with the filter still writing tags.

```yaml
extensions:
  social:
    enabled: no
```

```txt
(E) [social] enabled: must be of type "boolean", got "string".
```

:::

## What stays behind once the filter is off

The filter writes no tag, and every tag Quarto writes for the deck stays.
A deck in a Quarto website with `open-graph` and `twitter-card` turned on therefore keeps a card.
The [Reference](../reference.qmd#overlap-with-quarto) lists what each source contributes.

The extension still reads the rest of the configuration and reports what it cannot accept.
A misspelt key under `extensions.social` is reported while `enabled` is `false`.

## Leaving the filter out instead

A deck that never names the filter has nothing to switch off.

```yaml
filters:
  - social
```

Remove those two lines and the deck renders with the tags Quarto writes by itself.
The site builds one deck [with the filter](../preview.html) and one [without it](../preview-without.html), so the two heads can be compared.

::: {.callout-note}

## Removing the filter and setting `enabled: false` give the same head

Both routes leave Quarto's own tags in place and add nothing.
`enabled` is the route for a deck inside a project that names the filter in `_quarto.yml`.
That deck turns the filter off for itself, and every other deck in the project keeps its tags.
:::
